Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential theft:** No evidence was found of broad harvesting of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets. install.sh reads/writes its own ~/.agent-whatsapp/.env, which appears to be documented application configuration handling.
  • **Exfiltration/staging:** No evidence was found of tar/zip/base64 staging of harvested files or uploads to attacker-controlled external endpoints.
  • **Persistence:** scripts/install.sh creates ~/.config/systemd/user/$SERVICE_NAME.service and calls systemctl --user enable. However, this is an explicit, documented installation step for running the WhatsApp gateway as a service, and it is not paired with stealth, unauthorized automatic execution, or credential theft evidence.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence was found of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, CI/CD token, or GitHub Actions workflow manipulation behavior.
  • **Obfuscation/loaders:** No evidence was found of base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec-based obfuscated loaders or staged payload downloaders in the provided code. The observed subprocess usage is consistent with the documented purpose of launching codex/claude and the Node bridge.
